# bytecheck - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bytecheck/latest/target-redirect/bytecheck/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#bytecheck)bytecheck

bytecheck is a memory validation framework for Rust.

For some types, creating an invalid value immediately results in undefined behavior. This can cause some issues when trying to validate potentially invalid bytes, as just casting the bytes to your type can technically cause errors. This makes it difficult to write validation routines, because until you’re certain that the bytes represent valid values you cannot cast them.

bytecheck provides a framework for performing these byte-level validations and implements checks for basic types along with a derive macro to implement validation for custom structs and enums.

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

[ CheckBytes](https://docs.rs/trait.CheckBytes.html) is at the heart of bytecheck, and does the heavy lifting of
verifying that some bytes represent a valid type. Implementing it can be
done manually or automatically with the

[derive macro](https://docs.rs/derive.CheckBytes.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#layout-stability)Layout stability

The layouts of types may change between compiler versions, or even different
compilations. To guarantee stable type layout between compilations, structs,
enums, and unions can be annotated with `#[repr(C)]`, and enums specifically
can be annotated with `#[repr(int)]` or `#[repr(C, int)]` as well. See
[the reference’s page on type layout](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/type-layout.html) for more details.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- `derive`: Re-exports the macros from- `bytecheck_derive`. Enabled by default.
- `simdutf8`: Uses the- `simdutf8`crate to validate UTF-8 strings. Enabled by default.

[§](https://docs.rs#crates)Crates

Bytecheck provides integrations for some common crates by default. In the future, crates should depend on bytecheck and provide their own integration.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use bytecheck::{CheckBytes, check_bytes, rancor::Failure};
#[derive(CheckBytes, Debug)]
#[repr(C)]
struct Test {
    a: u32,
    b: char,
    c: bool,
}
#[repr(C, align(4))]
struct Aligned<const N: usize>([u8; N]);
macro_rules! bytes {
    ($($byte:literal,)*) => {
        (&Aligned([$($byte,)*]).0 as &[u8]).as_ptr()
    };
    ($($byte:literal),*) => {
        bytes!($($byte,)*)
    };
}
// In this example, the architecture is assumed to be little-endian
#[cfg(target_endian = "little")]
unsafe {
    // These are valid bytes for a `Test`
    check_bytes::<Test, Failure>(
        bytes![
            0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8,
            0x78u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8,
            1u8, 255u8, 255u8, 255u8,
        ].cast()
    ).unwrap();
    // Changing the bytes for the u32 is OK, any bytes are a valid u32
    check_bytes::<Test, Failure>(
        bytes![
            42u8, 16u8, 20u8, 3u8,
            0x78u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8,
            1u8, 255u8, 255u8, 255u8,
        ].cast()
    ).unwrap();
    // Characters outside the valid ranges are invalid
    check_bytes::<Test, Failure>(
        bytes![
            0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8,
            0x00u8, 0xd8u8, 0u8, 0u8,
            1u8, 255u8, 255u8, 255u8,
        ].cast()
    ).unwrap_err();
    check_bytes::<Test, Failure>(
        bytes![
            0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8,
            0x00u8, 0x00u8, 0x11u8, 0u8,
            1u8, 255u8, 255u8, 255u8,
        ].cast()
    ).unwrap_err();
    // 0 is a valid boolean value (false) but 2 is not
    check_bytes::<Test, Failure>(
        bytes![
            0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8,
            0x78u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8,
            0u8, 255u8, 255u8, 255u8,
        ].cast()
    ).unwrap();
    check_bytes::<Test, Failure>(
        bytes![
            0u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8,
            0x78u8, 0u8, 0u8, 0u8,
            2u8, 255u8, 255u8, 255u8,
        ].cast()
    ).unwrap_err();
}
```

# bytecheck/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! # bytecheck
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! bytecheck is a memory validation framework for Rust.
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//!
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! For some types, creating an invalid value immediately results in undefined
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! behavior. This can cause some issues when trying to validate potentially
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! invalid bytes, as just casting the bytes to your type can technically cause
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! errors. This makes it difficult to write validation routines, because until
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! you're certain that the bytes represent valid values you cannot cast them.
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//!
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! bytecheck provides a framework for performing these byte-level validations
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! and implements checks for basic types along with a derive macro to implement
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! validation for custom structs and enums.
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//!
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! ## Design
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//!
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! [`CheckBytes`] is at the heart of bytecheck, and does the heavy lifting of
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! verifying that some bytes represent a valid type. Implementing it can be
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! done manually or automatically with the [derive macro](macro@CheckBytes).
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//!
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! ## Layout stability
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//!
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//! The layouts of types may change between compiler versions, or even different
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//! compilations. To guarantee stable type layout between compilations, structs,
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//! enums, and unions can be annotated with `#[repr(C)]`, and enums specifically
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//! can be annotated with `#[repr(int)]` or `#[repr(C, int)]` as well. See
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! [the reference's page on type layout][reference] for more details.
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//!
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! [reference]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/type-layout.html
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//!
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! ## Features
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//!
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! - `derive`: Re-exports the macros from `bytecheck_derive`. Enabled by
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//!   default.
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! - `simdutf8`: Uses the `simdutf8` crate to validate UTF-8 strings. Enabled
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!   by default.
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//!
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! ### Crates
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! Bytecheck provides integrations for some common crates by default. In the
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! future, crates should depend on bytecheck and provide their own integration.
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! - [`uuid-1`](https://docs.rs/uuid/1)
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//!
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! ## Example

[101](https://docs.rs#101)#[cfg(feature = "simdutf8")]
[102](https://docs.rs#102)use simdutf8::basic::from_utf8;
[103](https://docs.rs#103)
[104](https://docs.rs#104)/// A type that can check whether a pointer points to a valid value.
[105](https://docs.rs#105)///
[106](https://docs.rs#106)/// `CheckBytes` can be derived with [`CheckBytes`](macro@CheckBytes) or
[107](https://docs.rs#107)/// implemented manually for custom behavior.
[108](https://docs.rs#108)///
[109](https://docs.rs#109)/// # Safety
[110](https://docs.rs#110)///
[111](https://docs.rs#111)/// `check_bytes` must only return `Ok` if `value` points to a valid instance of
[112](https://docs.rs#112)/// `Self`. Because `value` must always be properly aligned for `Self` and point
[113](https://docs.rs#113)/// to enough bytes to represent the type, this implies that `value` may be
[114](https://docs.rs#114)/// dereferenced safely.
[115](https://docs.rs#115)///
[116](https://docs.rs#116)/// # Example
[117](https://docs.rs#117)///
[118](https://docs.rs#118)/// ```
[119](https://docs.rs#119)/// use core::{error::Error, fmt};
[120](https://docs.rs#120)///
[121](https://docs.rs#121)/// use bytecheck::CheckBytes;
[122](https://docs.rs#122)/// use rancor::{fail, Fallible, Source};
[123](https://docs.rs#123)///
[124](https://docs.rs#124)/// #[repr(C, align(4))]
[125](https://docs.rs#125)/// pub struct NonMaxU32(u32);
[126](https://docs.rs#126)///
[127](https://docs.rs#127)/// unsafe impl<C: Fallible + ?Sized> CheckBytes<C> for NonMaxU32
[128](https://docs.rs#128)/// where
[129](https://docs.rs#129)///     C::Error: Source,
[130](https://docs.rs#130)/// {
[131](https://docs.rs#131)///     unsafe fn check_bytes(
[132](https://docs.rs#132)///         value: *const Self,
[133](https://docs.rs#133)///         context: &mut C,
[134](https://docs.rs#134)///     ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[135](https://docs.rs#135)///         #[derive(Debug)]
[136](https://docs.rs#136)///         struct NonMaxCheckError;
[137](https://docs.rs#137)///
[138](https://docs.rs#138)///         impl fmt::Display for NonMaxCheckError {
[139](https://docs.rs#139)///             fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[140](https://docs.rs#140)///                 write!(f, "non-max u32 was set to u32::MAX")
[141](https://docs.rs#141)///             }
[142](https://docs.rs#142)///         }
[143](https://docs.rs#143)///
[144](https://docs.rs#144)///         impl Error for NonMaxCheckError {}
[145](https://docs.rs#145)///
[146](https://docs.rs#146)///         let value = unsafe { value.read() };
[147](https://docs.rs#147)///         if value.0 == u32::MAX {
[148](https://docs.rs#148)///             fail!(NonMaxCheckError);
[149](https://docs.rs#149)///         }
[150](https://docs.rs#150)///
[151](https://docs.rs#151)///         Ok(())
[152](https://docs.rs#152)///     }
[153](https://docs.rs#153)/// }
[154](https://docs.rs#154)/// ```
[155](https://docs.rs#155)///
[156](https://docs.rs#156)/// See [`Verify`] for an example which uses less unsafe.
[157](https://docs.rs#157)pub unsafe trait CheckBytes<C: Fallible + ?Sized> {
[158](https://docs.rs#158)    /// Checks whether the given pointer points to a valid value within the
[159](https://docs.rs#159)    /// given context.
[160](https://docs.rs#160)    ///
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    /// # Safety
[162](https://docs.rs#162)    ///
[163](https://docs.rs#163)    /// The passed pointer must be aligned and point to enough initialized bytes
[164](https://docs.rs#164)    /// to represent the type.
[165](https://docs.rs#165)    unsafe fn check_bytes(
[166](https://docs.rs#166)        value: *const Self,
[167](https://docs.rs#167)        context: &mut C,
[168](https://docs.rs#168)    ) -> Result<(), C::Error>;
[169](https://docs.rs#169)}
[170](https://docs.rs#170)
[171](https://docs.rs#171)/// A type that can check whether its invariants are upheld.
[172](https://docs.rs#172)///
[173](https://docs.rs#173)/// When using [the derive](macro@CheckBytes), adding `#[bytecheck(verify)]`
[174](https://docs.rs#174)/// allows implementing `Verify` for the derived type. [`Verify::verify`] will
[175](https://docs.rs#175)/// be called after the type is checked and all fields are known to be valid.
[176](https://docs.rs#176)///
[177](https://docs.rs#177)/// # Safety
[178](https://docs.rs#178)///
[179](https://docs.rs#179)/// - `verify` must only return `Ok` if all of the invariants of this type are
[180](https://docs.rs#180)///   upheld by `self`.
[181](https://docs.rs#181)/// - `verify` may not assume that its type invariants are upheld by the given
[182](https://docs.rs#182)///   `self` (the invariants of each field are guaranteed to be upheld).
[183](https://docs.rs#183)///
[184](https://docs.rs#184)/// # Example
[185](https://docs.rs#185)///
[186](https://docs.rs#186)/// ```
[187](https://docs.rs#187)/// use core::{error::Error, fmt};
[188](https://docs.rs#188)///
[189](https://docs.rs#189)/// use bytecheck::{CheckBytes, Verify};
[190](https://docs.rs#190)/// use rancor::{fail, Fallible, Source};
[191](https://docs.rs#191)///
[192](https://docs.rs#192)/// #[derive(CheckBytes)]
[193](https://docs.rs#193)/// #[bytecheck(verify)]
[194](https://docs.rs#194)/// #[repr(C, align(4))]
[195](https://docs.rs#195)/// pub struct NonMaxU32(u32);
[196](https://docs.rs#196)///
[197](https://docs.rs#197)/// unsafe impl<C: Fallible + ?Sized> Verify<C> for NonMaxU32
[198](https://docs.rs#198)/// where
[199](https://docs.rs#199)///     C::Error: Source,
[200](https://docs.rs#200)/// {
[201](https://docs.rs#201)///     fn verify(&self, context: &mut C) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[202](https://docs.rs#202)///         #[derive(Debug)]
[203](https://docs.rs#203)///         struct NonMaxCheckError;
[204](https://docs.rs#204)///
[205](https://docs.rs#205)///         impl fmt::Display for NonMaxCheckError {
[206](https://docs.rs#206)///             fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[207](https://docs.rs#207)///                 write!(f, "non-max u32 was set to u32::MAX")
[208](https://docs.rs#208)///             }
[209](https://docs.rs#209)///         }
[210](https://docs.rs#210)///
[211](https://docs.rs#211)///         impl Error for NonMaxCheckError {}
[212](https://docs.rs#212)///
[213](https://docs.rs#213)///         if self.0 == u32::MAX {
[214](https://docs.rs#214)///             fail!(NonMaxCheckError);
[215](https://docs.rs#215)///         }
[216](https://docs.rs#216)///
[217](https://docs.rs#217)///         Ok(())
[218](https://docs.rs#218)///     }
[219](https://docs.rs#219)/// }
[220](https://docs.rs#220)/// ```
[221](https://docs.rs#221)pub unsafe trait Verify<C: Fallible + ?Sized> {
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    /// Checks whether the invariants of this type are upheld by `self`.
[223](https://docs.rs#223)    fn verify(&self, context: &mut C) -> Result<(), C::Error>;
[224](https://docs.rs#224)}
[225](https://docs.rs#225)
[226](https://docs.rs#226)/// Checks whether the given pointer points to a valid value.
[227](https://docs.rs#227)///
[228](https://docs.rs#228)/// # Safety
[229](https://docs.rs#229)///
[230](https://docs.rs#230)/// The passed pointer must be aligned and point to enough initialized bytes to
[231](https://docs.rs#231)/// represent the type.
[232](https://docs.rs#232)///
[233](https://docs.rs#233)/// # Example
[234](https://docs.rs#234)///
[235](https://docs.rs#235)/// ```
[236](https://docs.rs#236)/// use bytecheck::check_bytes;
[237](https://docs.rs#237)/// use rancor::Failure;
[238](https://docs.rs#238)///
[239](https://docs.rs#239)/// unsafe {
[240](https://docs.rs#240)///     // 0 and 1 are valid values for bools
[241](https://docs.rs#241)///     check_bytes::<bool, Failure>((&0u8 as *const u8).cast()).unwrap();
[242](https://docs.rs#242)///     check_bytes::<bool, Failure>((&1u8 as *const u8).cast()).unwrap();
[243](https://docs.rs#243)///
[244](https://docs.rs#244)///     // 2 is not a valid value
[245](https://docs.rs#245)///     check_bytes::<bool, Failure>((&2u8 as *const u8).cast()).unwrap_err();
[246](https://docs.rs#246)/// }
[247](https://docs.rs#247)/// ```
[248](https://docs.rs#248)#[inline]
[249](https://docs.rs#249)pub unsafe fn check_bytes<T, E>(value: *const T) -> Result<(), E>
[250](https://docs.rs#250)where
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    T: CheckBytes<Strategy<(), E>> + ?Sized,
[252](https://docs.rs#252){
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    // SAFETY: The safety conditions of `check_bytes_with_context` are the same
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    // as the safety conditions of this function.
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    unsafe { check_bytes_with_context(value, &mut ()) }
[256](https://docs.rs#256)}
[257](https://docs.rs#257)
[258](https://docs.rs#258)/// Checks whether the given pointer points to a valid value within the given
[259](https://docs.rs#259)/// context.
[260](https://docs.rs#260)///
[261](https://docs.rs#261)/// # Safety
[262](https://docs.rs#262)///
[263](https://docs.rs#263)/// The passed pointer must be aligned and point to enough initialized bytes to
[264](https://docs.rs#264)/// represent the type.
[265](https://docs.rs#265)///
[266](https://docs.rs#266)/// # Example
[267](https://docs.rs#267)///
[268](https://docs.rs#268)/// ```
[269](https://docs.rs#269)/// use core::{error::Error, fmt};
[270](https://docs.rs#270)///
[271](https://docs.rs#271)/// use bytecheck::{check_bytes_with_context, CheckBytes, Verify};
[272](https://docs.rs#272)/// use rancor::{fail, Failure, Fallible, Source, Strategy};
[273](https://docs.rs#273)///
[274](https://docs.rs#274)/// trait Context {
[275](https://docs.rs#275)///     fn is_allowed(&self, value: u8) -> bool;
[276](https://docs.rs#276)/// }
[277](https://docs.rs#277)///
[278](https://docs.rs#278)/// impl<T: Context + ?Sized, E> Context for Strategy<T, E> {
[279](https://docs.rs#279)///     fn is_allowed(&self, value: u8) -> bool {
[280](https://docs.rs#280)///         T::is_allowed(self, value)
[281](https://docs.rs#281)///     }
[282](https://docs.rs#282)/// }
[283](https://docs.rs#283)///
[284](https://docs.rs#284)/// struct Allowed(u8);
[285](https://docs.rs#285)///
[286](https://docs.rs#286)/// impl Context for Allowed {
[287](https://docs.rs#287)///     fn is_allowed(&self, value: u8) -> bool {
[288](https://docs.rs#288)///         value == self.0
[289](https://docs.rs#289)///     }
[290](https://docs.rs#290)/// }
[291](https://docs.rs#291)///
[292](https://docs.rs#292)/// #[derive(CheckBytes)]
[293](https://docs.rs#293)/// #[bytecheck(verify)]
[294](https://docs.rs#294)/// #[repr(C)]
[295](https://docs.rs#295)/// pub struct ContextualByte(u8);
[296](https://docs.rs#296)///
[297](https://docs.rs#297)/// unsafe impl<C: Context + Fallible + ?Sized> Verify<C> for ContextualByte
[298](https://docs.rs#298)/// where
[299](https://docs.rs#299)///     C::Error: Source,
[300](https://docs.rs#300)/// {
[301](https://docs.rs#301)///     fn verify(&self, context: &mut C) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[302](https://docs.rs#302)///         #[derive(Debug)]
[303](https://docs.rs#303)///         struct InvalidByte(u8);
[304](https://docs.rs#304)///
[305](https://docs.rs#305)///         impl fmt::Display for InvalidByte {
[306](https://docs.rs#306)///             fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[307](https://docs.rs#307)///                 write!(f, "invalid contextual byte: {}", self.0)
[308](https://docs.rs#308)///             }
[309](https://docs.rs#309)///         }
[310](https://docs.rs#310)///
[311](https://docs.rs#311)///         impl Error for InvalidByte {}
[312](https://docs.rs#312)///
[313](https://docs.rs#313)///         if !context.is_allowed(self.0) {
[314](https://docs.rs#314)///             fail!(InvalidByte(self.0));
[315](https://docs.rs#315)///         }
[316](https://docs.rs#316)///
[317](https://docs.rs#317)///         Ok(())
[318](https://docs.rs#318)///     }
[319](https://docs.rs#319)/// }
[320](https://docs.rs#320)///
[321](https://docs.rs#321)/// let value = 45u8;
[322](https://docs.rs#322)/// unsafe {
[323](https://docs.rs#323)///     // Checking passes when the context allows byte 45
[324](https://docs.rs#324)///     check_bytes_with_context::<ContextualByte, _, Failure>(
[325](https://docs.rs#325)///         (&value as *const u8).cast(),
[326](https://docs.rs#326)///         &mut Allowed(45),
[327](https://docs.rs#327)///     )
[328](https://docs.rs#328)///     .unwrap();
[329](https://docs.rs#329)///
[330](https://docs.rs#330)///     // Checking fails when the conteext does not allow byte 45
[331](https://docs.rs#331)///     check_bytes_with_context::<ContextualByte, _, Failure>(
[332](https://docs.rs#332)///         (&value as *const u8).cast(),
[333](https://docs.rs#333)///         &mut Allowed(0),
[334](https://docs.rs#334)///     )
[335](https://docs.rs#335)///     .unwrap_err();
[336](https://docs.rs#336)/// }
[337](https://docs.rs#337)/// ```
[338](https://docs.rs#338)pub unsafe fn check_bytes_with_context<T, C, E>(
[339](https://docs.rs#339)    value: *const T,
[340](https://docs.rs#340)    context: &mut C,
[341](https://docs.rs#341)) -> Result<(), E>
[342](https://docs.rs#342)where
[343](https://docs.rs#343)    T: CheckBytes<Strategy<C, E>> + ?Sized,
[344](https://docs.rs#344){
[345](https://docs.rs#345)    // SAFETY: The safety conditions of `check_bytes` are the same as the safety
[346](https://docs.rs#346)    // conditions of this function.
[347](https://docs.rs#347)    unsafe { CheckBytes::check_bytes(value, Strategy::wrap(context)) }

[352](https://docs.rs#352)        // SAFETY: All bit patterns are valid for these primitive types.
[353](https://docs.rs#353)        unsafe impl<C: Fallible + ?Sized> CheckBytes<C> for $type {

[358](https://docs.rs#358)            ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[359](https://docs.rs#359)                Ok(())
[360](https://docs.rs#360)            }
[361](https://docs.rs#361)        }
[362](https://docs.rs#362)    };

[397](https://docs.rs#397)// valid.
[398](https://docs.rs#398)unsafe impl<C: Fallible + ?Sized> CheckBytes<C> for PhantomPinned {
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    #[inline]

[404](https://docs.rs#404)
[405](https://docs.rs#405)// SAFETY: `ManuallyDrop<T>` is a `#[repr(transparent)]` wrapper around a `T`,
[406](https://docs.rs#406)// and so `value` points to a valid `ManuallyDrop<T>` if it also points to a
[407](https://docs.rs#407)// valid `T`.
[408](https://docs.rs#408)unsafe impl<T, C> CheckBytes<C> for ManuallyDrop<T>
[409](https://docs.rs#409)where
[410](https://docs.rs#410)    T: CheckBytes<C> + ?Sized,
[411](https://docs.rs#411)    C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[412](https://docs.rs#412)    C::Error: Trace,
[413](https://docs.rs#413){
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    #[inline]
[415](https://docs.rs#415)    unsafe fn check_bytes(
[416](https://docs.rs#416)        value: *const Self,
[417](https://docs.rs#417)        c: &mut C,
[418](https://docs.rs#418)    ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[419](https://docs.rs#419)        // SAFETY: Because `ManuallyDrop<T>` is `#[repr(transparent)]`, a
[420](https://docs.rs#420)        // pointer to a `ManuallyDrop<T>` is guaranteed to be the same as a
[421](https://docs.rs#421)        // pointer to `T`. We can't call `.cast()` here because `T` may be
[422](https://docs.rs#422)        // an unsized type.
[423](https://docs.rs#423)        let inner_ptr =
[424](https://docs.rs#424)            unsafe { core::mem::transmute::<*const Self, *const T>(value) };
[425](https://docs.rs#425)        // SAFETY: The caller has guaranteed that `value` is aligned for
[426](https://docs.rs#426)        // `ManuallyDrop<T>` and points to enough bytes to represent
[427](https://docs.rs#427)        // `ManuallyDrop<T>`. Since `ManuallyDrop<T>` is `#[repr(transparent)]`,
[428](https://docs.rs#428)        // `inner_ptr` is also aligned for `T` and points to enough bytes to
[429](https://docs.rs#429)        // represent it.
[430](https://docs.rs#430)        unsafe {
[431](https://docs.rs#431)            T::check_bytes(inner_ptr, c)
[432](https://docs.rs#432)                .trace("while checking inner value of `ManuallyDrop`")
[433](https://docs.rs#433)        }
[434](https://docs.rs#434)    }
[435](https://docs.rs#435)}
[436](https://docs.rs#436)
[437](https://docs.rs#437)// SAFETY: `UnsafeCell<T>` has the same memory layout as `T`, and so `value`
[438](https://docs.rs#438)// points to a valid `UnsafeCell<T>` if it also points to a valid `T`.
[439](https://docs.rs#439)unsafe impl<T, C> CheckBytes<C> for UnsafeCell<T>
[440](https://docs.rs#440)where
[441](https://docs.rs#441)    T: CheckBytes<C> + ?Sized,
[442](https://docs.rs#442)    C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[443](https://docs.rs#443)    C::Error: Trace,
[444](https://docs.rs#444){
[445](https://docs.rs#445)    #[inline]
[446](https://docs.rs#446)    unsafe fn check_bytes(
[447](https://docs.rs#447)        value: *const Self,
[448](https://docs.rs#448)        c: &mut C,
[449](https://docs.rs#449)    ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[450](https://docs.rs#450)        // SAFETY: Because `UnsafeCell<T>` has the same memory layout as
[451](https://docs.rs#451)        // `T`, a pointer to an `UnsafeCell<T>` is guaranteed to be the same
[452](https://docs.rs#452)        // as a pointer to `T`. We can't call `.cast()` here because `T` may
[453](https://docs.rs#453)        // be an unsized type.
[454](https://docs.rs#454)        let inner_ptr =
[455](https://docs.rs#455)            unsafe { core::mem::transmute::<*const Self, *const T>(value) };
[456](https://docs.rs#456)        // SAFETY: The caller has guaranteed that `value` is aligned for
[457](https://docs.rs#457)        // `UnsafeCell<T>` and points to enough bytes to represent
[458](https://docs.rs#458)        // `UnsafeCell<T>`. Since `UnsafeCell<T>` has the same layout `T`,
[459](https://docs.rs#459)        // `inner_ptr` is also aligned for `T` and points to enough bytes to
[460](https://docs.rs#460)        // represent it.
[461](https://docs.rs#461)        unsafe {
[462](https://docs.rs#462)            T::check_bytes(inner_ptr, c)
[463](https://docs.rs#463)                .trace("while checking inner value of `UnsafeCell`")
[464](https://docs.rs#464)        }
[465](https://docs.rs#465)    }
[466](https://docs.rs#466)}
[467](https://docs.rs#467)
[468](https://docs.rs#468)// SAFETY: `Cell<T>` has the same memory layout as `UnsafeCell<T>` (and
[469](https://docs.rs#469)// therefore `T` itself), and so `value` points to a valid `UnsafeCell<T>` if it
[470](https://docs.rs#470)// also points to a valid `T`.
[471](https://docs.rs#471)unsafe impl<T, C> CheckBytes<C> for Cell<T>
[472](https://docs.rs#472)where
[473](https://docs.rs#473)    T: CheckBytes<C> + ?Sized,
[474](https://docs.rs#474)    C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[475](https://docs.rs#475)    C::Error: Trace,
[476](https://docs.rs#476){
[477](https://docs.rs#477)    #[inline]
[478](https://docs.rs#478)    unsafe fn check_bytes(
[479](https://docs.rs#479)        value: *const Self,
[480](https://docs.rs#480)        c: &mut C,
[481](https://docs.rs#481)    ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[482](https://docs.rs#482)        // SAFETY: Because `Cell<T>` has the same memory layout as
[483](https://docs.rs#483)        // `UnsafeCell<T>` (and therefore `T` itself), a pointer to a
[484](https://docs.rs#484)        // `Cell<T>` is guaranteed to be the same as a pointer to `T`. We
[485](https://docs.rs#485)        // can't call `.cast()` here because `T` may be an unsized type.
[486](https://docs.rs#486)        let inner_ptr =
[487](https://docs.rs#487)            unsafe { core::mem::transmute::<*const Self, *const T>(value) };
[488](https://docs.rs#488)        // SAFETY: The caller has guaranteed that `value` is aligned for
[489](https://docs.rs#489)        // `Cell<T>` and points to enough bytes to represent `Cell<T>`. Since
[490](https://docs.rs#490)        // `Cell<T>` has the same layout as `UnsafeCell<T>` ( and therefore `T`
[491](https://docs.rs#491)        // itself), `inner_ptr` is also aligned for `T` and points to enough
[492](https://docs.rs#492)        // bytes to represent it.
[493](https://docs.rs#493)        unsafe {
[494](https://docs.rs#494)            T::check_bytes(inner_ptr, c)
[495](https://docs.rs#495)                .trace("while checking inner value of `Cell`")
[496](https://docs.rs#496)        }
[497](https://docs.rs#497)    }
[498](https://docs.rs#498)}
[499](https://docs.rs#499)
[500](https://docs.rs#500)#[derive(Debug)]
[501](https://docs.rs#501)struct BoolCheckError {
[502](https://docs.rs#502)    byte: u8,
[503](https://docs.rs#503)}
[504](https://docs.rs#504)
[505](https://docs.rs#505)impl fmt::Display for BoolCheckError {
[506](https://docs.rs#506)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[507](https://docs.rs#507)        write!(
[508](https://docs.rs#508)            f,
[509](https://docs.rs#509)            "bool set to invalid byte {}, expected either 0 or 1",
[510](https://docs.rs#510)            self.byte,
[511](https://docs.rs#511)        )
[512](https://docs.rs#512)    }
[513](https://docs.rs#513)}
[514](https://docs.rs#514)
[515](https://docs.rs#515)impl Error for BoolCheckError {}
[516](https://docs.rs#516)
[517](https://docs.rs#517)// SAFETY: A bool is a one byte value that must either be 0 or 1. `check_bytes`
[518](https://docs.rs#518)// only returns `Ok` if `value` is 0 or 1.
[519](https://docs.rs#519)unsafe impl<C> CheckBytes<C> for bool
[520](https://docs.rs#520)where
[521](https://docs.rs#521)    C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[522](https://docs.rs#522)    C::Error: Source,
[523](https://docs.rs#523){
[524](https://docs.rs#524)    #[inline]
[525](https://docs.rs#525)    unsafe fn check_bytes(
[526](https://docs.rs#526)        value: *const Self,
[527](https://docs.rs#527)        _: &mut C,
[528](https://docs.rs#528)    ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[529](https://docs.rs#529)        // SAFETY: `value` is a pointer to a `bool`, which has a size and
[530](https://docs.rs#530)        // alignment of one. `u8` also has a size and alignment of one, and all
[531](https://docs.rs#531)        // bit patterns are valid for `u8`. So we can cast `value` to a `u8`
[532](https://docs.rs#532)        // pointer and read from it.
[533](https://docs.rs#533)        let byte = unsafe { *value.cast::<u8>() };
[534](https://docs.rs#534)        match byte {
[535](https://docs.rs#535)            0 | 1 => Ok(()),
[536](https://docs.rs#536)            _ => fail!(BoolCheckError { byte }),
[537](https://docs.rs#537)        }
[538](https://docs.rs#538)    }
[539](https://docs.rs#539)}
[540](https://docs.rs#540)
[541](https://docs.rs#541)#[cfg(target_has_atomic = "8")]
[542](https://docs.rs#542)// SAFETY: `AtomicBool` has the same ABI as `bool`, so if `value` points to a
[543](https://docs.rs#543)// valid `bool` then it also points to a valid `AtomicBool`.
[544](https://docs.rs#544)unsafe impl<C> CheckBytes<C> for AtomicBool
[545](https://docs.rs#545)where
[546](https://docs.rs#546)    C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[547](https://docs.rs#547)    C::Error: Source,
[548](https://docs.rs#548){
[549](https://docs.rs#549)    #[inline]
[550](https://docs.rs#550)    unsafe fn check_bytes(
[551](https://docs.rs#551)        value: *const Self,
[552](https://docs.rs#552)        context: &mut C,
[553](https://docs.rs#553)    ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[554](https://docs.rs#554)        // SAFETY: `AtomicBool` has the same ABI as `bool`, so a pointer that is
[555](https://docs.rs#555)        // aligned for `AtomicBool` and points to enough bytes for `AtomicBool`
[556](https://docs.rs#556)        // is also aligned for `bool` and points to enough bytes for `bool`.
[557](https://docs.rs#557)        unsafe { bool::check_bytes(value.cast(), context) }
[558](https://docs.rs#558)    }
[559](https://docs.rs#559)}
[560](https://docs.rs#560)
[561](https://docs.rs#561)// SAFETY: If `char::try_from` succeeds with the pointed-to-value, then it must
[562](https://docs.rs#562)// be a valid value for `char`.
[563](https://docs.rs#563)unsafe impl<C> CheckBytes<C> for char
[564](https://docs.rs#564)where
[565](https://docs.rs#565)    C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[566](https://docs.rs#566)    C::Error: Source,
[567](https://docs.rs#567){
[568](https://docs.rs#568)    #[inline]
[569](https://docs.rs#569)    unsafe fn check_bytes(ptr: *const Self, _: &mut C) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[570](https://docs.rs#570)        // SAFETY: `char` and `u32` are both four bytes, but we're not
[571](https://docs.rs#571)        // guaranteed that they have the same alignment. Using `read_unaligned`
[572](https://docs.rs#572)        // ensures that we can read a `u32` regardless and try to convert it to
[573](https://docs.rs#573)        // a `char`.
[574](https://docs.rs#574)        let value = unsafe { ptr.cast::<u32>().read_unaligned() };
[575](https://docs.rs#575)        char::try_from(value).into_error()?;
[576](https://docs.rs#576)        Ok(())
[577](https://docs.rs#577)    }
[578](https://docs.rs#578)}
[579](https://docs.rs#579)
[580](https://docs.rs#580)#[derive(Debug)]
[581](https://docs.rs#581)struct TupleIndexContext {
[582](https://docs.rs#582)    index: usize,
[583](https://docs.rs#583)}
[584](https://docs.rs#584)
[585](https://docs.rs#585)impl fmt::Display for TupleIndexContext {
[586](https://docs.rs#586)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[587](https://docs.rs#587)        write!(f, "while checking index {} of tuple", self.index)
[588](https://docs.rs#588)    }
[589](https://docs.rs#589)}
[590](https://docs.rs#590)
[591](https://docs.rs#591)macro_rules! impl_tuple {
[592](https://docs.rs#592)    ($($type:ident $index:tt),*) => {
[593](https://docs.rs#593)        // SAFETY: A tuple is valid if all of its elements are valid, and
[594](https://docs.rs#594)        // `check_bytes` only returns `Ok` when all of the elements validated
[595](https://docs.rs#595)        // successfully.
[596](https://docs.rs#596)        unsafe impl<$($type,)* C> CheckBytes<C> for ($($type,)*)
[597](https://docs.rs#597)        where
[598](https://docs.rs#598)            $($type: CheckBytes<C>,)*
[599](https://docs.rs#599)            C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[600](https://docs.rs#600)            C::Error: Trace,
[601](https://docs.rs#601)        {
[602](https://docs.rs#602)            #[inline]
[603](https://docs.rs#603)            #[allow(clippy::unneeded_wildcard_pattern)]
[604](https://docs.rs#604)            unsafe fn check_bytes(
[605](https://docs.rs#605)                value: *const Self,
[606](https://docs.rs#606)                context: &mut C,
[607](https://docs.rs#607)            ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[608](https://docs.rs#608)                $(
[609](https://docs.rs#609)                    // SAFETY: The caller has guaranteed that `value` points to
[610](https://docs.rs#610)                    // enough bytes for this tuple and is properly aligned, so
[611](https://docs.rs#611)                    // we can create pointers to each element and check them.
[612](https://docs.rs#612)                    unsafe {
[613](https://docs.rs#613)                        <$type>::check_bytes(
[614](https://docs.rs#614)                            ptr::addr_of!((*value).$index),
[615](https://docs.rs#615)                            context,
[616](https://docs.rs#616)                        ).with_trace(|| TupleIndexContext { index: $index })?;
[617](https://docs.rs#617)                    }
[618](https://docs.rs#618)                )*
[619](https://docs.rs#619)                Ok(())
[620](https://docs.rs#620)            }
[621](https://docs.rs#621)        }
[622](https://docs.rs#622)    }
[623](https://docs.rs#623)}
[624](https://docs.rs#624)

[627](https://docs.rs#627)impl_tuple!(T0 0, T1 1, T2 2);

[644](https://docs.rs#644)#[derive(Debug)]
[645](https://docs.rs#645)struct ArrayCheckContext {
[646](https://docs.rs#646)    index: usize,
[647](https://docs.rs#647)}
[648](https://docs.rs#648)
[649](https://docs.rs#649)impl fmt::Display for ArrayCheckContext {
[650](https://docs.rs#650)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[651](https://docs.rs#651)        write!(f, "while checking index '{}' of array", self.index)
[652](https://docs.rs#652)    }
[653](https://docs.rs#653)}
[654](https://docs.rs#654)
[655](https://docs.rs#655)// SAFETY: `check_bytes` only returns `Ok` if each element of the array is
[656](https://docs.rs#656)// valid. If each element of the array is valid then the whole array is also
[657](https://docs.rs#657)// valid.
[658](https://docs.rs#658)unsafe impl<T, const N: usize, C> CheckBytes<C> for [T; N]
[659](https://docs.rs#659)where
[660](https://docs.rs#660)    T: CheckBytes<C>,
[661](https://docs.rs#661)    C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[662](https://docs.rs#662)    C::Error: Trace,
[663](https://docs.rs#663){
[664](https://docs.rs#664)    #[inline]
[665](https://docs.rs#665)    unsafe fn check_bytes(
[666](https://docs.rs#666)        value: *const Self,
[667](https://docs.rs#667)        context: &mut C,
[668](https://docs.rs#668)    ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[669](https://docs.rs#669)        let base = value.cast::<T>();
[670](https://docs.rs#670)        for index in 0..N {
[671](https://docs.rs#671)            // SAFETY: The caller has guaranteed that `value` points to enough
[672](https://docs.rs#672)            // bytes for this array and is properly aligned, so we can create
[673](https://docs.rs#673)            // pointers to each element and check them.
[674](https://docs.rs#674)            unsafe {
[675](https://docs.rs#675)                T::check_bytes(base.add(index), context)
[676](https://docs.rs#676)                    .with_trace(|| ArrayCheckContext { index })?;
[677](https://docs.rs#677)            }
[678](https://docs.rs#678)        }
[679](https://docs.rs#679)        Ok(())
[680](https://docs.rs#680)    }
[681](https://docs.rs#681)}
[682](https://docs.rs#682)
[683](https://docs.rs#683)#[derive(Debug)]
[684](https://docs.rs#684)struct SliceCheckContext {
[685](https://docs.rs#685)    index: usize,
[686](https://docs.rs#686)}
[687](https://docs.rs#687)
[688](https://docs.rs#688)impl fmt::Display for SliceCheckContext {
[689](https://docs.rs#689)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[690](https://docs.rs#690)        write!(f, "while checking index '{}' of slice", self.index)
[691](https://docs.rs#691)    }
[692](https://docs.rs#692)}
[693](https://docs.rs#693)
[694](https://docs.rs#694)// SAFETY: `check_bytes` only returns `Ok` if each element of the slice is
[695](https://docs.rs#695)// valid. If each element of the slice is valid then the whole slice is also
[696](https://docs.rs#696)// valid.
[697](https://docs.rs#697)unsafe impl<T, C> CheckBytes<C> for [T]
[698](https://docs.rs#698)where
[699](https://docs.rs#699)    T: CheckBytes<C>,
[700](https://docs.rs#700)    C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[701](https://docs.rs#701)    C::Error: Trace,
[702](https://docs.rs#702){
[703](https://docs.rs#703)    #[inline]
[704](https://docs.rs#704)    unsafe fn check_bytes(
[705](https://docs.rs#705)        value: *const Self,
[706](https://docs.rs#706)        context: &mut C,
[707](https://docs.rs#707)    ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[708](https://docs.rs#708)        let (data_address, len) = ptr_meta::to_raw_parts(value);
[709](https://docs.rs#709)        let base = data_address.cast::<T>();
[710](https://docs.rs#710)        for index in 0..len {
[711](https://docs.rs#711)            // SAFETY: The caller has guaranteed that `value` points to enough
[712](https://docs.rs#712)            // bytes for this slice and is properly aligned, so we can create
[713](https://docs.rs#713)            // pointers to each element and check them.
[714](https://docs.rs#714)            unsafe {
[715](https://docs.rs#715)                T::check_bytes(base.add(index), context)
[716](https://docs.rs#716)                    .with_trace(|| SliceCheckContext { index })?;
[717](https://docs.rs#717)            }
[718](https://docs.rs#718)        }
[719](https://docs.rs#719)        Ok(())
[720](https://docs.rs#720)    }
[721](https://docs.rs#721)}
[722](https://docs.rs#722)
[723](https://docs.rs#723)// SAFETY: `check_bytes` only returns `Ok` if the bytes pointed to by `str` are
[724](https://docs.rs#724)// valid UTF-8. If they are valid UTF-8 then the overall `str` is also valid.
[725](https://docs.rs#725)unsafe impl<C> CheckBytes<C> for str
[726](https://docs.rs#726)where
[727](https://docs.rs#727)    C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[728](https://docs.rs#728)    C::Error: Source,
[729](https://docs.rs#729){
[730](https://docs.rs#730)    #[inline]
[731](https://docs.rs#731)    unsafe fn check_bytes(
[732](https://docs.rs#732)        value: *const Self,
[733](https://docs.rs#733)        _: &mut C,
[734](https://docs.rs#734)    ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[735](https://docs.rs#735)        #[derive(Debug)]
[736](https://docs.rs#736)        struct Utf8Error;
[737](https://docs.rs#737)
[738](https://docs.rs#738)        impl fmt::Display for Utf8Error {
[739](https://docs.rs#739)            fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[740](https://docs.rs#740)                write!(f, "invalid UTF-8")
[741](https://docs.rs#741)            }
[742](https://docs.rs#742)        }
[743](https://docs.rs#743)
[744](https://docs.rs#744)        impl Error for Utf8Error {}
[745](https://docs.rs#745)
[746](https://docs.rs#746)        let slice_ptr = value as *const [u8];
[747](https://docs.rs#747)        // SAFETY: The caller has guaranteed that `value` is properly-aligned
[748](https://docs.rs#748)        // and points to enough bytes for its `str`. Because a `u8` slice has
[749](https://docs.rs#749)        // the same layout as a `str`, we can dereference it for UTF-8
[750](https://docs.rs#750)        // validation.
[751](https://docs.rs#751)        let slice = unsafe { &*slice_ptr };
[752](https://docs.rs#752)
[753](https://docs.rs#753)        // Checking whether a byte slice is ASCII is much faster than checking
[754](https://docs.rs#754)        // whether it is valid UTF-8. Falling back to a full UTF-8 check
[755](https://docs.rs#755)        // afterward nets a performance improvement for the average case.
[756](https://docs.rs#756)        if !slice.is_ascii() {
[757](https://docs.rs#757)            from_utf8(slice).map_err(|_| Utf8Error).into_error()?;
[758](https://docs.rs#758)        }
[759](https://docs.rs#759)
[760](https://docs.rs#760)        Ok(())
[761](https://docs.rs#761)    }
[762](https://docs.rs#762)}
[763](https://docs.rs#763)
[764](https://docs.rs#764)// SAFETY: `check_bytes` only returns `Ok` when the bytes constitute a valid
[765](https://docs.rs#765)// `CStr` per `CStr::from_bytes_with_nul`.
[766](https://docs.rs#766)unsafe impl<C> CheckBytes<C> for CStr
[767](https://docs.rs#767)where
[768](https://docs.rs#768)    C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[769](https://docs.rs#769)    C::Error: Source,
[770](https://docs.rs#770){
[771](https://docs.rs#771)    #[inline]
[772](https://docs.rs#772)    unsafe fn check_bytes(
[773](https://docs.rs#773)        value: *const Self,
[774](https://docs.rs#774)        _: &mut C,
[775](https://docs.rs#775)    ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[776](https://docs.rs#776)        let slice_ptr = value as *const [u8];
[777](https://docs.rs#777)        // SAFETY: The caller has guaranteed that `value` is properly-aligned
[778](https://docs.rs#778)        // and points to enough bytes for its `CStr`. Because a `u8` slice has
[779](https://docs.rs#779)        // the same layout as a `CStr`, we can dereference it for validation.
[780](https://docs.rs#780)        let slice = unsafe { &*slice_ptr };
[781](https://docs.rs#781)        CStr::from_bytes_with_nul(slice).into_error()?;
[782](https://docs.rs#782)        Ok(())
[783](https://docs.rs#783)    }
[784](https://docs.rs#784)}
[785](https://docs.rs#785)

[907](https://docs.rs#907)
[908](https://docs.rs#908)// Range types
[909](https://docs.rs#909)
[910](https://docs.rs#910)// SAFETY: A `Range<T>` is valid if its `start` and `end` are both valid, and
[911](https://docs.rs#911)// `check_bytes` only returns `Ok` when both `start` and `end` are valid. Note
[912](https://docs.rs#912)// that `Range` does not require `start` be less than `end`.
[913](https://docs.rs#913)unsafe impl<T, C> CheckBytes<C> for ops::Range<T>
[914](https://docs.rs#914)where
[915](https://docs.rs#915)    T: CheckBytes<C>,
[916](https://docs.rs#916)    C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[917](https://docs.rs#917)    C::Error: Trace,
[918](https://docs.rs#918){
[919](https://docs.rs#919)    #[inline]
[920](https://docs.rs#920)    unsafe fn check_bytes(
[921](https://docs.rs#921)        value: *const Self,
[922](https://docs.rs#922)        context: &mut C,
[923](https://docs.rs#923)    ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[924](https://docs.rs#924)        // SAFETY: The caller has guaranteed that `value` is aligned for a
[925](https://docs.rs#925)        // `Range<T>` and points to enough initialized bytes for one, so a
[926](https://docs.rs#926)        // pointer projected to the `start` field will be properly aligned for
[927](https://docs.rs#927)        // a `T` and point to enough initialized bytes for one too.
[928](https://docs.rs#928)        unsafe {
[929](https://docs.rs#929)            T::check_bytes(ptr::addr_of!((*value).start), context).with_trace(
[930](https://docs.rs#930)                || StructCheckContext {
[931](https://docs.rs#931)                    struct_name: "Range",
[932](https://docs.rs#932)                    field_name: "start",
[933](https://docs.rs#933)                },
[934](https://docs.rs#934)            )?;
[935](https://docs.rs#935)        }
[936](https://docs.rs#936)        // SAFETY: Same reasoning as above, but for `end`.
[937](https://docs.rs#937)        unsafe {
[938](https://docs.rs#938)            T::check_bytes(ptr::addr_of!((*value).end), context).with_trace(
[939](https://docs.rs#939)                || StructCheckContext {
[940](https://docs.rs#940)                    struct_name: "Range",
[941](https://docs.rs#941)                    field_name: "end",
[942](https://docs.rs#942)                },
[943](https://docs.rs#943)            )?;
[944](https://docs.rs#944)        }
[945](https://docs.rs#945)        Ok(())
[946](https://docs.rs#946)    }
[947](https://docs.rs#947)}
[948](https://docs.rs#948)
[949](https://docs.rs#949)// SAFETY: A `RangeFrom<T>` is valid if its `start` is valid, and `check_bytes`
[950](https://docs.rs#950)// only returns `Ok` when its `start` is valid.
[951](https://docs.rs#951)unsafe impl<T, C> CheckBytes<C> for ops::RangeFrom<T>
[952](https://docs.rs#952)where
[953](https://docs.rs#953)    T: CheckBytes<C>,
[954](https://docs.rs#954)    C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[955](https://docs.rs#955)    C::Error: Trace,
[956](https://docs.rs#956){
[957](https://docs.rs#957)    #[inline]
[958](https://docs.rs#958)    unsafe fn check_bytes(
[959](https://docs.rs#959)        value: *const Self,
[960](https://docs.rs#960)        context: &mut C,
[961](https://docs.rs#961)    ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[962](https://docs.rs#962)        // SAFETY: The caller has guaranteed that `value` is aligned for a
[963](https://docs.rs#963)        // `RangeFrom<T>` and points to enough initialized bytes for one, so a
[964](https://docs.rs#964)        // pointer projected to the `start` field will be properly aligned for
[965](https://docs.rs#965)        // a `T` and point to enough initialized bytes for one too.
[966](https://docs.rs#966)        unsafe {
[967](https://docs.rs#967)            T::check_bytes(ptr::addr_of!((*value).start), context).with_trace(
[968](https://docs.rs#968)                || StructCheckContext {
[969](https://docs.rs#969)                    struct_name: "RangeFrom",
[970](https://docs.rs#970)                    field_name: "start",
[971](https://docs.rs#971)                },
[972](https://docs.rs#972)            )?;
[973](https://docs.rs#973)        }
[974](https://docs.rs#974)        Ok(())
[975](https://docs.rs#975)    }
[976](https://docs.rs#976)}
[977](https://docs.rs#977)

[980](https://docs.rs#980)    #[inline]
[981](https://docs.rs#981)    unsafe fn check_bytes(_: *const Self, _: &mut C) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[982](https://docs.rs#982)        Ok(())

[999](https://docs.rs#999)        // SAFETY: The caller has guaranteed that `value` is aligned for a
[1000](https://docs.rs#1000)        // `RangeTo<T>` and points to enough initialized bytes for one, so a
[1001](https://docs.rs#1001)        // pointer projected to the `end` field will be properly aligned for
[1002](https://docs.rs#1002)        // a `T` and point to enough initialized bytes for one too.

[1015](https://docs.rs#1015)// SAFETY: A `RangeToInclusive<T>` is valid if its `end` is valid, and
[1016](https://docs.rs#1016)// `check_bytes` only returns `Ok` when its `end` is valid.
[1017](https://docs.rs#1017)unsafe impl<T, C> CheckBytes<C> for ops::RangeToInclusive<T>
[1018](https://docs.rs#1018)where
[1019](https://docs.rs#1019)    T: CheckBytes<C>,
[1020](https://docs.rs#1020)    C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[1021](https://docs.rs#1021)    C::Error: Trace,
[1022](https://docs.rs#1022){
[1023](https://docs.rs#1023)    #[inline]
[1024](https://docs.rs#1024)    unsafe fn check_bytes(
[1025](https://docs.rs#1025)        value: *const Self,
[1026](https://docs.rs#1026)        context: &mut C,
[1027](https://docs.rs#1027)    ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[1028](https://docs.rs#1028)        // SAFETY: The caller has guaranteed that `value` is aligned for a
[1029](https://docs.rs#1029)        // `RangeToInclusive<T>` and points to enough initialized bytes for one,
[1030](https://docs.rs#1030)        // so a pointer projected to the `end` field will be properly aligned
[1031](https://docs.rs#1031)        // for a `T` and point to enough initialized bytes for one too.
[1032](https://docs.rs#1032)        unsafe {
[1033](https://docs.rs#1033)            T::check_bytes(ptr::addr_of!((*value).end), context).with_trace(
[1034](https://docs.rs#1034)                || StructCheckContext {
[1035](https://docs.rs#1035)                    struct_name: "RangeToInclusive",
[1036](https://docs.rs#1036)                    field_name: "end",
[1037](https://docs.rs#1037)                },
[1038](https://docs.rs#1038)            )?;
[1039](https://docs.rs#1039)        }
[1040](https://docs.rs#1040)        Ok(())
[1041](https://docs.rs#1041)    }

[1044](https://docs.rs#1044)#[derive(Debug)]
[1045](https://docs.rs#1045)struct NonZeroCheckError;
[1046](https://docs.rs#1046)
[1047](https://docs.rs#1047)impl fmt::Display for NonZeroCheckError {
[1048](https://docs.rs#1048)    #[inline]
[1049](https://docs.rs#1049)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
[1050](https://docs.rs#1050)        write!(f, "nonzero integer is zero")
[1051](https://docs.rs#1051)    }
[1052](https://docs.rs#1052)}
[1053](https://docs.rs#1053)
[1054](https://docs.rs#1054)impl Error for NonZeroCheckError {}
[1055](https://docs.rs#1055)
[1056](https://docs.rs#1056)macro_rules! impl_nonzero {
[1057](https://docs.rs#1057)    ($nonzero:ident, $underlying:ident) => {
[1058](https://docs.rs#1058)        // SAFETY: `check_bytes` only returns `Ok` when `value` is not zero, the
[1059](https://docs.rs#1059)        // only validity condition for non-zero integer types.
[1060](https://docs.rs#1060)        unsafe impl<C> CheckBytes<C> for $nonzero
[1061](https://docs.rs#1061)        where
[1062](https://docs.rs#1062)            C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[1063](https://docs.rs#1063)            C::Error: Source,
[1064](https://docs.rs#1064)        {
[1065](https://docs.rs#1065)            #[inline]
[1066](https://docs.rs#1066)            unsafe fn check_bytes(
[1067](https://docs.rs#1067)                value: *const Self,
[1068](https://docs.rs#1068)                _: &mut C,
[1069](https://docs.rs#1069)            ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[1070](https://docs.rs#1070)                // SAFETY: Non-zero integer types are guaranteed to have the
[1071](https://docs.rs#1071)                // same ABI as their corresponding integer types. Those integers
[1072](https://docs.rs#1072)                // have no validity requirements, so we can cast and dereference
[1073](https://docs.rs#1073)                // value to check if it is equal to zero.
[1074](https://docs.rs#1074)                if unsafe { *value.cast::<$underlying>() } == 0 {
[1075](https://docs.rs#1075)                    fail!(NonZeroCheckError);
[1076](https://docs.rs#1076)                } else {
[1077](https://docs.rs#1077)                    Ok(())
[1078](https://docs.rs#1078)                }
[1079](https://docs.rs#1079)            }
[1080](https://docs.rs#1080)        }
[1081](https://docs.rs#1081)    };
[1082](https://docs.rs#1082)}
[1083](https://docs.rs#1083)
[1084](https://docs.rs#1084)impl_nonzero!(NonZeroI8, i8);
[1085](https://docs.rs#1085)impl_nonzero!(NonZeroI16, i16);
[1086](https://docs.rs#1086)impl_nonzero!(NonZeroI32, i32);
[1087](https://docs.rs#1087)impl_nonzero!(NonZeroI64, i64);
[1088](https://docs.rs#1088)impl_nonzero!(NonZeroI128, i128);
[1089](https://docs.rs#1089)impl_nonzero!(NonZeroU8, u8);

[1091](https://docs.rs#1091)impl_nonzero!(NonZeroU32, u32);

[1259](https://docs.rs#1259)    fn test_c_str() {
[1260](https://docs.rs#1260)        macro_rules! test_cases {
[1261](https://docs.rs#1261)            ($($bytes:expr, $pat:pat,)*) => {
[1262](https://docs.rs#1262)                $(
[1263](https://docs.rs#1263)                    let bytes = $bytes;
[1264](https://docs.rs#1264)                    let c_str = ::ptr_meta::from_raw_parts(
[1265](https://docs.rs#1265)                        bytes.as_ptr().cast(),
[1266](https://docs.rs#1266)                        bytes.len(),
[1267](https://docs.rs#1267)                    );
[1268](https://docs.rs#1268)                    assert!(matches!(
[1269](https://docs.rs#1269)                        check_bytes::<CStr, Failure>(c_str),
[1270](https://docs.rs#1270)                        $pat,
[1271](https://docs.rs#1271)                    ));
[1272](https://docs.rs#1272)                )*
[1273](https://docs.rs#1273)            }
[1274](https://docs.rs#1274)        }
[1275](https://docs.rs#1275)

[1580](https://docs.rs#1580)    #[test]
[1581](https://docs.rs#1581)    fn test_recursive() {
[1582](https://docs.rs#1582)        struct MyBox<T: ?Sized> {
[1583](https://docs.rs#1583)            inner: *const T,
[1584](https://docs.rs#1584)        }
[1585](https://docs.rs#1585)
[1586](https://docs.rs#1586)        unsafe impl<T, C> CheckBytes<C> for MyBox<T>
[1587](https://docs.rs#1587)        where
[1588](https://docs.rs#1588)            T: CheckBytes<C>,
[1589](https://docs.rs#1589)            C: Fallible + ?Sized,
[1590](https://docs.rs#1590)        {
[1591](https://docs.rs#1591)            unsafe fn check_bytes(
[1592](https://docs.rs#1592)                value: *const Self,
[1593](https://docs.rs#1593)                context: &mut C,
[1594](https://docs.rs#1594)            ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
[1595](https://docs.rs#1595)                unsafe { T::check_bytes((*value).inner, context) }
[1596](https://docs.rs#1596)            }
[1597](https://docs.rs#1597)        }
[1598](https://docs.rs#1598)
[1599](https://docs.rs#1599)        #[allow(dead_code)]
[1600](https://docs.rs#1600)        #[derive(CheckBytes)]
[1601](https://docs.rs#1601)        #[bytecheck(crate)]
[1602](https://docs.rs#1602)        #[repr(u8)]
[1603](https://docs.rs#1603)        enum Node {
[1604](https://docs.rs#1604)            Nil,
[1605](https://docs.rs#1605)            Cons(#[bytecheck(omit_bounds)] MyBox<Node>),
[1606](https://docs.rs#1606)        }
[1607](https://docs.rs#1607)
[1608](https://docs.rs#1608)        unsafe {
[1609](https://docs.rs#1609)            let nil = Node::Nil;
[1610](https://docs.rs#1610)            let cons = Node::Cons(MyBox {

# CheckBytes in bytecheck - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bytecheck/latest/target-redirect/bytecheck/trait.CheckBytes.html

`pub unsafe trait CheckBytes<C: `[Fallible](https://docs.rs/rancor/0.1.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/rancor/trait.Fallible.html) + ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)> {
    // Required method
    unsafe fn [check_bytes](https://docs.rs#tymethod.check_bytes)(
        value: [*const ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)Self,
        context: [&mut C](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.reference.html),
    ) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.unit.html), C::[Error](https://docs.rs/rancor/0.1.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/rancor/trait.Fallible.html#associatedtype.Error)>;
}## Expand description

A type that can check whether a pointer points to a valid value.

`CheckBytes` can be derived with [ CheckBytes](https://docs.rs/derive.CheckBytes.html) or
implemented manually for custom behavior.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

`check_bytes` must only return `Ok` if `value` points to a valid instance of
`Self`. Because `value` must always be properly aligned for `Self` and point
to enough bytes to represent the type, this implies that `value` may be
dereferenced safely.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use core::{error::Error, fmt};
use bytecheck::CheckBytes;
use rancor::{fail, Fallible, Source};
#[repr(C, align(4))]
pub struct NonMaxU32(u32);
unsafe impl<C: Fallible + ?Sized> CheckBytes<C> for NonMaxU32
where
    C::Error: Source,
{
    unsafe fn check_bytes(
        value: *const Self,
        context: &mut C,
    ) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
        #[derive(Debug)]
        struct NonMaxCheckError;
        impl fmt::Display for NonMaxCheckError {
            fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
                write!(f, "non-max u32 was set to u32::MAX")
            }
        }
        impl Error for NonMaxCheckError {}
        let value = unsafe { value.read() };
        if value.0 == u32::MAX {
            fail!(NonMaxCheckError);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
```
See [ Verify](https://docs.rs/trait.Verify.html) for an example which uses less unsafe.

## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# CheckBytes in bytecheck - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bytecheck/latest/target-redirect/bytecheck/derive.CheckBytes.html

```
#[derive(CheckBytes)]
{
    // Attributes available to this derive:
    #[bytecheck]
}
```
## Expand description

Derives `CheckBytes` for the labeled type.

This derive macro automatically adds a type bound `field: CheckBytes<__C>`
for each field type. This can cause an overflow while evaluating trait
bounds if the structure eventually references its own type, as the
implementation of `CheckBytes` for a struct depends on each field type
implementing it as well. Adding the attribute `#[check_bytes(omit_bounds)]`
to a field will suppress this trait bound and allow recursive structures.
This may be too coarse for some types, in which case additional type bounds
may be required with `bounds(...)`.

[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)Attributes

Additional arguments can be specified using attributes.

`#[bytecheck(...)]` accepts the following attributes:

[§](https://docs.rs#types-only)Types only

- `bounds(...)`: Adds additional bounds to the- `CheckBytes`implementation. This can be especially useful when dealing with recursive structures, where bounds may need to be omitted to prevent recursive type definitions. In the context of the added bounds,- `__C`is the name of the context generic (e.g.- `__C: MyContext`).
- `crate = ...`: Chooses an alternative crate path to import bytecheck from.
- `verify`: Adds an additional verification step after the validity of each field has been checked. See the- `Verify`trait for more information.

[§](https://docs.rs#fields-only)Fields only

- `omit_bounds`: Omits trait bounds for the annotated field in the generated impl.

---

# NamedEnumVariantCheckContext in bytecheck - Rust

pub struct NamedEnumVariantCheckContext {

```

    pub field_name: &'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html),

Context for errors resulting from checking enum variants with named fields.

This context is used by the derive macro to trace which field of an enum variant failed validation.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.field_name)

`field_name: &'static `[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.str.html)The name of the field that was invalid.

# Verify in bytecheck - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bytecheck/latest/target-redirect/bytecheck/trait.Verify.html

`pub unsafe trait Verify<C: `[Fallible](https://docs.rs/rancor/0.1.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/rancor/trait.Fallible.html) + ?[Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)> {
    // Required method
    fn [verify](https://docs.rs#tymethod.verify)(&self, context: [&mut C](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.reference.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.unit.html), C::[Error](https://docs.rs/rancor/0.1.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/rancor/trait.Fallible.html#associatedtype.Error)>;
}## Expand description

A type that can check whether its invariants are upheld.

When using [the derive](https://docs.rs/derive.CheckBytes.html), adding `#[bytecheck(verify)]`
allows implementing `Verify` for the derived type. [ Verify::verify](https://docs.rs/trait.Verify.html#tymethod.verify) will
be called after the type is checked and all fields are known to be valid.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

- `verify`must only return- `Ok`if all of the invariants of this type are upheld by- `self`.
- `verify`may not assume that its type invariants are upheld by the given- `self`(the invariants of each field are guaranteed to be upheld).

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use core::{error::Error, fmt};
use bytecheck::{CheckBytes, Verify};
use rancor::{fail, Fallible, Source};
#[derive(CheckBytes)]
#[bytecheck(verify)]
#[repr(C, align(4))]
pub struct NonMaxU32(u32);
unsafe impl<C: Fallible + ?Sized> Verify<C> for NonMaxU32
where
    C::Error: Source,
{
    fn verify(&self, context: &mut C) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
        #[derive(Debug)]
        struct NonMaxCheckError;
        impl fmt::Display for NonMaxCheckError {
            fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
                write!(f, "non-max u32 was set to u32::MAX")
            }
        }
        impl Error for NonMaxCheckError {}
        if self.0 == u32::MAX {
            fail!(NonMaxCheckError);
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
```
## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://docs.rs#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

# check_bytes in bytecheck - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bytecheck/latest/target-redirect/bytecheck/fn.check_bytes.html

## Expand description

Checks whether the given pointer points to a valid value.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

The passed pointer must be aligned and point to enough initialized bytes to represent the type.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use bytecheck::check_bytes;
use rancor::Failure;
unsafe {
    // 0 and 1 are valid values for bools
    check_bytes::<bool, Failure>((&0u8 as *const u8).cast()).unwrap();
    check_bytes::<bool, Failure>((&1u8 as *const u8).cast()).unwrap();
    // 2 is not a valid value
    check_bytes::<bool, Failure>((&2u8 as *const u8).cast()).unwrap_err();
}
```

---

# check_bytes_with_context in bytecheck - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/bytecheck/latest/target-redirect/bytecheck/fn.check_bytes_with_context.html

```
pub unsafe fn check_bytes_with_context<T, C, E>(
    value:
```
[*const T](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html),
    context: [&mut C](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.reference.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.unit.html), E>## Expand description

Checks whether the given pointer points to a valid value within the given context.

[§](https://docs.rs#safety)Safety

The passed pointer must be aligned and point to enough initialized bytes to represent the type.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use core::{error::Error, fmt};
use bytecheck::{check_bytes_with_context, CheckBytes, Verify};
use rancor::{fail, Failure, Fallible, Source, Strategy};
trait Context {
    fn is_allowed(&self, value: u8) -> bool;
}
impl<T: Context + ?Sized, E> Context for Strategy<T, E> {
    fn is_allowed(&self, value: u8) -> bool {
        T::is_allowed(self, value)
    }
}
struct Allowed(u8);
impl Context for Allowed {
    fn is_allowed(&self, value: u8) -> bool {
        value == self.0
    }
}
#[derive(CheckBytes)]
#[bytecheck(verify)]
#[repr(C)]
pub struct ContextualByte(u8);
unsafe impl<C: Context + Fallible + ?Sized> Verify<C> for ContextualByte
where
    C::Error: Source,
{
    fn verify(&self, context: &mut C) -> Result<(), C::Error> {
        #[derive(Debug)]
        struct InvalidByte(u8);
        impl fmt::Display for InvalidByte {
            fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
                write!(f, "invalid contextual byte: {}", self.0)
            }
        }
        impl Error for InvalidByte {}
        if !context.is_allowed(self.0) {
            fail!(InvalidByte(self.0));
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}
let value = 45u8;
unsafe {
    // Checking passes when the context allows byte 45
    check_bytes_with_context::<ContextualByte, _, Failure>(
        (&value as *const u8).cast(),
        &mut Allowed(45),
    )
    .unwrap();
    // Checking fails when the conteext does not allow byte 45
    check_bytes_with_context::<ContextualByte, _, Failure>(
        (&value as *const u8).cast(),
        &mut Allowed(0),
    )
    .unwrap_err();
}
```

---

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
- [clap-verbosity-flag](https://crates.io/crates/clap-verbosity-flag)
- [clap-cargo](https://crates.io/crates/clap-cargo)
- [colorchoice-clap](https://crates.io/crates/colorchoice-clap)

Testing

- `trycmd`
- `snapbox`
- `assert_cmd`- `assert_fs`

Documentation:

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [arg](https://docs.rs/macro.arg.html)
- Create an `Arg`
- [command](https://docs.rs/macro.command.html)- `cargo`
- Allows you to build the `Command`instance from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_authors.html)- authors - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the authors for the command from your Cargo.toml at
compile time in the form:
`"author1 lastname <author1@example.com>:author2 lastname <author2@example.com>"`
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_description.html)- description - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the description from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_name.html)- name - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the name from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_version.html)- version - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the version from your Cargo.toml at compile time as
`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH_PKGVERSION_PRE`
- [value_](https://docs.rs/macro.value_parser.html)- parser
- Select a `ValueParser`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Arg](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html)
- The abstract representation of a command line argument. Used to set all the options and relationships that define a valid argument for the program.
- [ArgGroup](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgGroup.html)
- Specifies a logical group of [arguments](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html)
- [ArgMatches](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html)
- Container for parse results.
- [Command](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- Build a command-line interface.
- [Id](https://docs.rs/struct.Id.html)
- `Arg`- `ArgGroup`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [ArgAction](https://docs.rs/enum.ArgAction.html)
- Behavior of arguments when they are encountered while parsing
- [Color](https://docs.rs/enum.ColorChoice.html)- Choice
- Represents the color preferences for program output
- [Value](https://docs.rs/enum.ValueHint.html)- Hint
- Provide shell with hint on how to complete an argument.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Args](https://docs.rs/trait.Args.html)
- Parse a set of arguments into a user-defined container.
- [Command](https://docs.rs/trait.CommandFactory.html)- Factory
- Create a `Command`
- [From](https://docs.rs/trait.FromArgMatches.html)- ArgMatches
- Converts an instance of `ArgMatches`
- [Parser](https://docs.rs/trait.Parser.html)
- Parse command-line arguments into `Self`.
- [Subcommand](https://docs.rs/trait.Subcommand.html)
- Parse a sub-command into a user-defined enum.
- [Value](https://docs.rs/trait.ValueEnum.html)- Enum
- Parse arguments into enums.

```
use clap::Parser;

    #[arg(short, long)]

    /// Number of times to greet

    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
